% Pattern: proof/manual/article. Two theorems, each followed by a manual
% proof head with no end mark. The first head ends at the second theorem, so
% each head proves the theorem before it.
% Seen in the gold pilot (set E).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1 status=here labels=th:a
% want head-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want theorem-2 statement/theorem 2 status=here labels=th:b
% want head-2 proof - proves=theorem-2
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newcommand{\off}[1]{}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem}\label{th:a}
A statement.
\end{theorem}

{\em Proof:} The proof for Theorem~\ref{th:a} is given later.

\begin{theorem}\label{th:b}
Another statement.
\end{theorem}
\off{An old argument.}

{\em Proof:} The proof for Theorem~\ref{th:b} is given later.

\section{More}
Some text.
\end{document}
